question.title: When will weekly U.S. regular retail gasoline prices first surpass $4.25 per gallon?
question.description:
The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) publishes weekly updates on national retail gasoline prices every Monday (or Tuesday in the event of federal holidays). This metric serves as a key indicator of consumer energy costs and inflation trends. Retail prices are highly sensitive to global crude oil supply, refinery capacity, and seasonal demand shifts.

This question tracks the national average price for regular gasoline across all formulations.
question.resolution_criteria:
If a price strictly exceeding \$4.25 is reported in the EIA series "Weekly U.S. Regular All Formulations Retail Gasoline Prices" (Series ID: EMM\_EPMR\_PTE\_NUS\_DPG) for a date on or before 2026-08-12T12:00:00+00:00 (`range_max_utc`), the question resolves as the ISO 8601 datetime (at 23:59:59 UTC) of the first such date listed in the series' "Date" column. If a qualifying price is reported but the date is not publicly verifiable to at least daily precision (e.g., only the month or quarter is reported), the question is annulled. If no qualifying price is reported for a date on or before 2026-08-12T12:00:00+00:00, the question resolves as >2026-08-12T12:00:00+00:00.

Data source: [EIA Petroleum & Other Liquids database](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET\&s=EMM_EPMR_PTE_NUS_DPG\&f=W). Resolution will be determined by the data as first reported in the weekly release. Subsequent retrospective revisions by the EIA to previously published weekly figures will be considered immaterial and will not alter the resolution outcome. The date used for resolution is the literal date string as it appears in the 'Date' column of the 'History' table at the linked EIA URL. This column historically tracks the Monday survey date, even when the release is delayed (e.g., due to federal holidays) and regardless of how the date is labeled in other EIA interfaces or API responses (e.g., as 'Week ending'). In the event of any discrepancy between the table's 'Date' column and the actual reporting or release date, the literal date string in the 'Date' column takes precedence.
